cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. I've put your umbrella back in the stand. You'll want it for work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. I gave it a rinse. I'll dry the handle before you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's pondweed caught in the spokes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it needs another rinse. Have breakfast; I'll get it back in the stand properly this time.

mechanism: A treats signs of its covert umbrella restoration as a pupil inspection exercise while suppressing how the object became dirty.
confusable: Not just denying blame: A keeps taking practical steps to return the object usable under a maintenance pretext.
comparison: Cleaning a suspiciously wet umbrella versus replacing a mismatched plate without explaining the missing original.
seedUse: Use D37 stand/wet/pondweed; S05 taking credit for observation distracts from what caused the evidence.
